# Through Time & Tide

Over many centuries, our iconic tidal island has attracted traders, pilgrims, fisherfolk and tales of giants and angels. Explore the cobbled streets of an historic village, beneath the ramparts of a legendary castle. Your island experience awaits…

* * *

- [Low Tide](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/#low-tide)
- [Mid Tide](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/#mid-tide)
- [High Tide](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/#high-tide)

## Visit an ancient tidal island in Cornwall and explore the cobbled streets of an historic village, beneath the ramparts of a legendary castle and terraced subtropical gardens.

[Summit Experiences](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/winter/) [Walking Calendar](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/getting-here/walking/) [Festive Afternoon Tea](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/shopping-eating/festive-afternoon-tea/) [Christmas Afternoon Tea](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/shopping-eating/christmas-afternoon-tea/)

## Winter on the Mount

During the winter, access is free to all visitors. The island only opens when the tide allows and the causeway is clear. Step into a world of history, myth and legend. Discover the shops, café, art gallery, harbour and village.

[What's open](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/opening-times-2026-27/)

![](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Pink-Mount-1.jpg)

![Christmas Afternoon Tea at Harbour Loft, St Michael's Mount](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/HarbourLoftAutumn-66-1800x1200.webp)

## Festive Afternoon Tea

Celebrate the festive season with Afternoon Tea on St Michael’s Mount. Enjoy seasonal treats created by Head Chef Marcus Houghton in a unique setting, with complimentary summit experiences included in every booking.

[Find out more](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/shopping-eating/festive-afternoon-tea/)

## Winter summit experiences

Climb to the castle summit and take in breathtaking panoramic views across Mount’s Bay from the historic battlements. At the top, discover more about the castle and its fascinating history through engaging talks led by knowledgeable senior guides.

[find out more](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/winter/)

![](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Extreme_weeding_at_St_Michaels_Mount_website_size-1800x1197.jpg)

![Harold Harvey - Tulip Pickers - St Michael's Mount](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Harold_Harvey_-_tulip_pickers_TH-crop-1800x1187.webp)

## Step back in time

Discover how life was lived in west Cornwall before the mid-20th century at the Steward's House Art Gallery. Home to the Sheila Hichens Collection, the gallery showcases works by Newlyn School artists, capturing the everyday lives, landscapes and communities of the time.

[find out more](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/explore-the-mount/the-stewards-house/)

# Walking the causeway

At low tide, you can use the ancient causeway to walk across to the island. Step onto the cobbles and tread a path followed by pilgrims, traders, nobles and villagers over many hundreds of years. The causeway is cobbled, uneven and tricky to navigate, please check our [accessibility information](https://stmichaelsmount.co.uk/plan-your-visit/access/) before you visit. For your own safety, please be aware that attempting to cross the causeway outside of the suggested times can be hazardous. When the causeway is submerged, it can limit visibility, the path is uneven, there can be strong currents and the sea rises quickly.

**Winter opening hours vary. See the Access Calendar below for dates and times.**

## When can I use the causeway?

During winter opening hours, at low tide, the causeway is revealed and visitors can stroll across and back. The causeway is open for around four hours each day, depending on the tides and weather.

You’ll need around 15 minutes to walk the length of the causeway.
